results.title: Global Survival: Put the ocean at the centre of COP31
results.description: For over 30 years, Pacific island countries have issued the same warning at the annual United Nations Climate Change Conference: the warming ocean threatens not just food and energy security, but global survival itself. And almost every year, our warning has been treated as a regional problem, a challenge confined to remote small islands and thus not warranting more than lip service from international leaders.

results.title: The CPKC Holiday Train is travelling through Quebec and here's where you can see it
results.description: Looking for a festive way to get into the Christmas spirit? You're in for a treat -- one of Canada's most magical Christmas traditions is making its way back to the province. The CPKC Holiday Train is returning for 2026, bringing with it a dazzling display of Christmas lights, festive music and plenty of holiday cheer. The train is back for what will be its 28th year, bringing communities together to fight food insecurity and helping local organizations provide meals and support during the holiday season. The brightly decorated train will travel through Quebec in November, making several stops where visitors can enjoy free live performances and get into the holiday spirit. Between the train decked out in holiday lights and the festive entertainment, this is one Christmas event you'll absolutely want to have on your radar. Here's where you can catch the CPKC Holiday Train in Quebec this year. CPKC Holiday Train stops in Quebec for 2026 The U.S. Holiday Train will kick things off in Canada in Montreal and Beaconsfield, while the Canada Holiday Train will begin in Lac-Mégantic, Quebec, on November 23rd before continuing on to Sherbrooke and Farnham later the same day. Then, on the 24th, the train will make its way through Kahnawake, Saint-Constant, Delson, Saint-Mathieu, and Lacolle in the Montérégie region. The Holiday Train will then make several stops in New York before ending its Quebec leg in the suburb of Dorion. Here's the complete schedule: Thursday, November 19, 2026: Montreal West, Quebec: 7 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. at Montreal West EXO Commuter Station Beaconsfield, Quebec: 8:30 p.m. to 9 p.m. at Beaconsfield EXO Commuter Station Monday, November 23, 2026: Lac-Mégantic, Quebec: 12 p.m. to 12:30 p.m. at Rue Cartier between Rue Lemieux & Rue American Authors and Rafaëlle RoyMaisonneuve Sherbrooke, Quebec: 4:45 p.m. to 5:15 p.m. at 795 Rue de la Rand at the CPKC Station Parking Farnham, Quebec: 8:30 p.m. to 9 p.m. at 191 Rue Victoria Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Kahnawake, Quebec: 5 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. at Old Malone Road Saint-Constant, Quebec: 6 p.m. to 6:30 p.m. at the rail crossing at Sainte Catherine St, on the east side of Sainte Catherine EXO Station Delson, Quebec: 6:55 p.m. to 7:20 p.m. at 1 Chemin de la Gare Saint-Mathieu, Quebec: 7:50 p.m. to 8:15 p.m. at École Jacques-Barclay at 368 Rue Principale Lacolle, Quebec: 9 p.m. to 9:30 p.m. at 10 Rue Sainte-Marie Saturday, November 28, 2026: Dorion, Quebec: 11:30 a.m. to 12 p.m. at 3101 Blvd. De La Gare, Vaudreuil/Dorion XO Station (gravel parking lot) Each stop features a free outdoor concert, with the train serving as the backdrop for the show. The 2026 Canadian tour features a lineup of artists including Owen Riegling, Sam Roberts Band, American Authors and Rafaëlle Roy, among others. Artists American Authors and Rafaëlle Roy will perform at each Quebec stop, with the exception of Montreal West and Beaconsfield, when artists Magic! and MARIS will perform. The train is in each city for only about 30 minutes, so be sure to arrive with enough time to find a good viewing spot. The best part is that there's no admission fee to attend the holiday performances. However, visitors are encouraged to bring non-perishable food or make a donation to their local food bank or pantry, and food bank representatives will be on-site collecting donations. Since 1999, the Holiday Train program has raised more than $28.3 million and collected over 5.6 million pounds of food for community food banks across Canada and the United States. If you do decide to attend a CPKC Holiday Train event, remember to bundle up as the events are held outdoors. CPKC also reminds visitors to stay at least 15 metres away from railway tracks and never stand on the tracks or railway gravel while taking photos. Price: Free to attend When: Select dates from November 23 -28, 2026 Address: Multiple locations in Quebec Why You Need To Go: You can see a brightly decorated holiday train for free in Quebec this Christmas season, and give back to the community while doing so. CPKC Holiday Train website Before you get going, check out our Responsible Travel Guide so you can be informed, be safe, be smart, and most of all, be respectful on your trip.

results.title: LIFE IN NAPLES - Heart to Heart: Hearts Around the Table
results.description: Heart to Heart Hearts Around the Table November 1, 2026 by LifeInNaples Thanksgiving marks the beginning of the holiday season. It has a way of bringing us back to what matters: traditions new and old, the gathering of family and friends, and, of course, a festive table filled with food. For some, preparation of a favorite recipe may be a poignant reminder of a loved one who passed. In the spirit of the season, it’s worth remembering that having enough food on the table isn’t something everyone in our community can take for granted. These are challenging times for many. The rising cost of everyday necessities, such as food and gas for starters, puts financial pressure at the forefront. And while the holidays tend to bring these needs into sharper focus, food insecurity and hardship don’t take a holiday. Perhaps this is where gratitude takes on a little more meaning. It doesn’t require us to overlook the challenges around us or to put on rose-colored glasses. Rather, we are invited to recognizewhat we have in this moment and consider how we might share a little of it with someone else. Over the years, I’ve highlighted the efforts of many local organizations and the caring people behind them, to bring these groups to the attention of our readers. Their work reminds me that lifting others up doesn’t always require a grand gesture. Sometimes it’s a meal, a volunteer afternoon, a financial contribution, or simply knowing where someone can turn when life becomes overwhelming. Sometimes, the first step is calling for assistance. It’s a reminder that caring for our community takes many forms. Sometimes it’s providing a meal; sometimes it’s helping a family find stability; and sometimes it’s making sure a child has a safe place to begin healing. As we gather around our own tables this Thanksgiving, perhaps we can make a little room in our thoughts for those whose circumstances are different from ours. We don’t have to solve every problem or support every cause. We can start with one organization, one volunteer opportunity or one small act of kindness. Gratitude isn’t simply about appreciating what we have. It’s also about recognizing that what we have can help others as well. Perhaps that’s one of the most meaningful ways to give thanks. Email Karen at Napleskcc@gmail.com to share suggestions for future columns. Please consider giving her a follow @Naplesbythenumbers on Instagram for more slices of Life in Naples The Collier Resource Center (239.434.2030) has long been an important resource for individuals and families navigating difficult circumstances. Beyond helping connect people with food, the organization serves as a bridge to other essential services, including housing, health care and assistance with everyday needs. When someone is unsure where to begin, having a knowledgeable resource to help navigate the options can make all the difference. There is also something special about people coming together to make a difference. Meals of Hope (239.596.8990) is a wonderful example of hands-on generosity. Its meal-packing events bring volunteers in service around a shared purpose, while its other hunger-relief initiatives help get food into the hands of those who need it. It’s a reminder that giving doesn’t always have to be complicated. Sometimes it starts with showing up, rolling up your sleeves and doing something tangible. The Harry Chapin Food Bank of Southwest Florida (239.330.7007) plays another critical role in addressing hunger throughout our region. Behind every food distribution is an extensive network of donors, volunteers and community partners working to make sure food reaches families, children and individuals facing food insecurity. The work of this organization reminds us that addressing hunger requires more than a single meal or a seasonal food drive; it takes a sustained community effort. And, sometimes the challenges facing our neighbors extend well beyond their grocery bill. The Hunger & Homeless Coalition of Collier County (239.263.9363) works with community partners to address homelessness, housing instability and related needs. Food insecurity and housing insecurity are almost always connected, and helping someone move toward greater stability can required addressing several challenges at once. Not every kind of nourishment comes from a kitchen. The Empowerment Farm (239.330.2777)offers another perspective on what it means to strengthen a community. Through its connection to animals, agriculture, and hands-on learning, the organization creates opportunities for people of different ages and abilities to experience connection in nature. Its work also reminds us of the importance of understanding where our food comes from and the value of bringing people (and animals) together on the land. A privilege of writing this column is discovering that the story doesn’t necessarily end when the article does. The Children’s Advocacy Center of Collier County (239.263.8383) is another organization I’ve introduced to readers in the past. Celebrating its 40th year in 2026, the Center continues its important work helping children and families affected by trauma and abuse through advocacy, therapy and coordinated services.
